headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict: Plandex can modify code and git state while social-auto-upload can push content to external platforms, creating unsafe default handoff paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A and B do not show a documented shared channel, but A can read/write project files and B consumes files for uploads, so a manual copy-paste or file handoff could carry malicious instructions. The pathway is unusual and not default, so low fits better than medium.
conditions: IF the operator copies A-generated text into B's upload inputs or account files
IF B parses file content as instructions rather than inert media metadata
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories
Review any text copied from A before pasting into B
Use a plain-text staging file with a human review step
Disable any auto-import of generated instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches source code and has broad network egress; B touches video, images, and account data and also has broad network egress. Even without a shared filesystem, a workflow that moves code, media, or account artifacts between them can expose sensitive project or account data in default use, so the interaction is plausible and not just unusual.
conditions: IF the same workspace or export bundle is used for both agents
IF B uploads files that A prepared containing secrets or internal code
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for code and media
Strip secrets from any files before transfer
Confirm upload targets before running B
Rotate any exposed account tokens immediately
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and modify git state, while B can write account-side content through upload workflows even though it cannot write local files. The overlap is not identical, but both can mutate shared project outputs, so conflicting edits and race conditions are plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or release bundle
IF B uploads artifacts that A is simultaneously rewriting
mitigations: Serialize edits through one operator
Freeze the repo before running B
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Check for stale files before upload
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces code changes and plans that B could treat as ready-to-publish artifacts, while B has downstream action-taking authority via external uploads. If B trusts A's output without verification, a bad plan or malformed asset can be propagated to public platforms, making the blast radius potentially irreversible and dangerous by default.
conditions: IF B uploads or publishes artifacts generated by A without human review
IF A's proposed changes are used as the source of truth for B's release step
mitigations: Require human approval before any publish step
Compare A's output against the source files
Run B only on a reviewed export bundle
Keep a rollback copy of published assets
requires-engineering: add validation gates before upload

E_compliance.rationale: A handles model provider API keys and source code, while B handles account data and media content. The profiles do not document residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven; uncertainty pushes this above low. The risk is mainly about unverified handling of account data across two distinct services.
conditions: IF account data from B is stored or logged by A's workspace
IF either service retains uploaded artifacts longer than the operator expects
mitigations: Review retention settings for both tools
Avoid placing account data in A's code workspace
Delete temporary upload artifacts after use
Document which service stores which data class
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
